newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to buy up to 200,000 tns rice from China.
newsitem.headline: Manila to buy up to 200,000 tns rice from China.

text.p: State-owned National Food Authority (NFA) had signed a contract to buy up to 200,000 tonnes of rice from China, a senior official of the Philippine Department of Agriculture said on Wednesday.

"The NFA has signed an agreement to buy 100,000 tonnes of China rice. The contract also stipulated an option for NFA to buy another 100,000 tonnes," the official who requested not to be named told Reuters.
The official declined to say at what price the Philippines bought the rice from China.
But the Philippine Star newspaper quoted NFA administrator Joemarie Gerochi as saying on Tuesday China agreed to sell 100,000 tonnes of rice at $291.50 per tonne.
Last month, the Philippines had clinched a deal to buy up to 110,000 tonnes of yellow corn from China at $157 per tonne C&F.
President Fidel Ramos authorised the NFA early this month to buy up to 650,000 tonnes of rice from neighbouring countries to shore up the Philippine rice buffer stocks before July.
Rice supply in the Philippines is traditionally low in the third quarter.
